subject: POC env preflight: org seeds, API tokens, IP allowlist, VPC peering & close plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Liz Martin <liz.martin@healthcore.com>, ops+infra@healthcore.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC env preflight: org seeds, API tokens, IP allowlist, VPC peering & close plan

Hi Liz / HealthCore infra team,

Following our MAP review this morning, attaching a concise preflight checklist so we can lock the POC window and hit the evaluation milestones. High-level asks for environment prep (target dry-run week: Sep 27):

1) Org & access:
- Please create a HealthCore "redwood-poc" org (or provide owner/admin) and share the org ID with us. This lets us seed service accounts and audit logs.
- List the primary contacts and their emails for IAM provisioning (we'll need one infra admin and two engineer readers).

2) API keys & token handling:
- We will provision scoped API tokens from our side that are short-lived for the POC. To support rotation during tests, confirm whether HealthCore wants us to pin key egress IPs or use token-based CIDR restrictions.

3) Network: IP allowlist & VPC peering
- Preferred: VPC peering (private) between HealthCore VPC and our POC VPC. If peering isn't possible, provide egress IP ranges for allowlisting.
- Please share the VPC CIDR blocks you expect to peer and your preferred maintenance window.

4) Compliance & procurement touchpoints:
- Any procurement/PO steps we should anticipate during the POC close (billing contact + PO cadence)?

5) Acceptance dry-run
- Proposed dry-run: Sep 27 10:00-11:30 PT (verify) — we'll run token rotation, a prefix-caching test, and an RTT measurement across the peered path.

I've also included a simple vpc-peering template and API key provisioning doc as stubs we can iterate on (see attachments). If this list looks good, please reply with the org ID, CIDRs for peering/allowlist, and the preferred PO contact by EOD Thu 9/16 so we can begin seeding.

Thanks — aiming for a smooth evaluation and clean close.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

---
Attachments: vpc-peering-template.txt (text), api-key-provisioning-instructions.md (md)

Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. A few notes from our side:

- Org: we'll create the redwood-poc org and assign myself (liz.martin@healthcore.com) as owner and infra@healthcore.com as the admin. Expect the org ID by EOD Thu 9/16.

- CIDRs: we're running in us-west-2. Our primary VPC CIDR is 10.20.0.0/16 and we have a transit VPC at 10.100.0.0/16; preferred peering would be to the transit VPC. I attached the spreadsheet (network CIDRs) to this reply for clarity.

- Peering vs allowlist: we prefer private peering but need to validate with network security. If peering is delayed, we'll provide egress IP ranges — target window for allowlist preflight is Sep 24.

- Procurement: billing contact is sara.kim@healthcore.com; procurement needs a simple Statement of Work and a small proof-of-concept invoice. I'll loop them in after the org ID is confirmed.

- Dry-run: Sep 27 works in principle; can we do 10:30 PT instead? That buys our on-call a bit more time.

I'll follow up with a firewall ticket number for allowlisting if peering isn't approved by next Wed.

Cheers,
Liz Martin
Head of Infrastructure | HealthCore
liz.martin@healthcore.com

Alex / Neha — quick internal notes before we finalize the doc to send to HealthCore: 

- If they're peering to the transit VPC (10.100.0.0/16) we should plan for asymmetric routing checks and provide a short checklist for route propagation. I'll draft the checklist and the exact peering request fields (region, accepter account ID, route table IDs).

- API tokens: propose to use short-lived scoped API keys (8 hour TTL) for the evaluation with automatic rotation; include an option to issue long-lived read-only tokens if procurement demands them. Need confirmation on whether HealthCore's firewall will block outbound 443 to our ephemeral endpoints. If so, we must provide static egress ranges.

- I'll prepare two templates: one for a pure VPC peering flow and one fallback for public egress allowlisting (with the exact IP blocks).

I'll attach the peering template and a short runbook draft to the outgoing message.

Thanks,
